title: The same pattern, flipped
idea: Opener: finding the smallest is the SAME best-so-far pattern as the biggest (Unit 59) — you just replace when something is SMALLER. Thinking first.

exercises.prompt: Last unit you found the BIGGEST by keeping a best-so-far and replacing it when you met something bigger. To find the SMALLEST, what changes?
options: Replace the best-so-far when you meet something SMALLER instead of bigger
Nothing at all — it is a brand new idea
exercises.explanation: Min is the SAME pattern as max, just flipped: replace on smaller, not bigger. You already know the shape — you only change the comparison.

exercises.prompt: Finding the smallest reuses the best-so-far idea from the biggest; only the comparison flips.
exercises.explanation: Same loop, same 'keep one best-so-far' shape. The only change is > becomes <. That is the whole unit.

exercises.prompt: Max replaced best when 'n > best'. For the smallest, the test becomes...
exercises.explanation: Flip the > to <. Now best is replaced only when n is SMALLER, so you end up with the minimum.

exercises.prompt: Where should the 'smallest so far' start, just like the biggest did?
options: At the first value in the list
At the length of the list
exercises.explanation: Same safe start as max: the first value. It is guaranteed to be a real value, so negatives and small numbers compare correctly.

exercises.prompt: Find the smallest of [4, 9, 2] by hand. Put the 'smallest so far' after each step in order (start with the first value, 4).
blocks: 2 is smaller than 4, smallest so far = 2
exercises.explanation: Start 4, 9 does not beat it (we want smaller), 2 does -> 2. The smallest is 2. Same walk as max, flipped rule.
2 is the smallest; it replaced the best-so-far on the last step.

exercises.prompt: Which real questions are 'find the smallest'? (pick all)
exercises.explanation: Coldest and cheapest both ask for the single smallest value. Total is a sum; 'the most' is a max.

exercises.prompt: For the smallest, you leave the best-so-far unchanged when the new value is NOT smaller.
exercises.explanation: Mirror image of max: only replace on a win. For min, a win means the new value is smaller.

exercises.prompt: You walk [6, 1, 8, 3] keeping the SMALLEST so far. What does it end at?
exercises.explanation: Start 6; 1 is smaller -> 1; 8 and 3 are not smaller than 1. The smallest is 1.

options: Track the smallest-so-far (max's pattern, flipped) to find the smallest value
exercises.explanation: Same best-so-far loop as the biggest, with the comparison flipped to find the smallest.
